text:
The Oilers walked into Newark carrying a three-game winning streak and left without it. The Devils won in a shootout, 4-3, after Arseny Gritsyuk scored in the fourth round and Kasperi Kapanen was stopped to end it. Jack Hughes, the first player taken in the 2019 draft, was the night's first star with two goals and an assist, one of them on a snap shot our model gave only a 4% chance of going in.

The scoreboard undersold how lopsided this was. NJD attempted 71 shots to EDM's 44 and had the better of the chances overall, 3.22 expected goals (a measure of shot quality) to 1.96. Our simulations of every shot give the Devils a 72% chance of winning a game played this way. The second period decided the game's shape: NJD outchanced EDM 1.67 to 0.17 and scored three times, including Connor Brown's power-play goal and Hughes's two. Evan Bouchard had opened the scoring with a slap shot in the first, but Edmonton spent much of the middle frame defending.

The Oilers hung on because their power play answered. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins scored late in the second and Leon Draisaitl tied it 54 seconds into the third, both with the man advantage, and Tristan Jarry finished 0.22 goals better than expected. Connor Hellebuyck was 1.04 goals worse than expected, though he stopped Colton Dach's 24% look in overtime. NJD takes the extra point and a win it earned on the chance count. EDM's winning streak ends at three, with a point to show for it.
